#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=HN_15
#   --qos=normal
#   -c 6
#   --mem=20G
#   --gres=gpu:a40:1
#   --time=13:59:00
#   --output=HN_15/slurm-%j.out
#   --error=HN_15/slurm-%j.err

#flux: --job-name=HN_15
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 6
#flux: --time-limit=13h59m

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=20G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:a40:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU (or without an A40), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=normal
# Flux QoS/priority mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Environment Setup
module purge
module load python/3.12.0
pip3 install --upgrade pip
pip3 install -U -q pandas numpy tensorflow cuda-python torch torchvision seaborn plotly matplotlib ipywidgets tqdm

# Run Experiments
python3 main.py --data_index 15

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 A40 GPU (`--gres=gpu:a40:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 20G of memory (`--mem=20G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
issues: Installing large packages at runtime (`pip3 install ... tensorflow torch ...`) can be slow and may exceed the allocated time; consider a pre-built environment or cached wheels.
